claim: Temporal focusing uses a diffraction grating to separate the spectral components of a pulsed laser beam, resulting in a temporally broadened pulse that is inefficient at excitation except at the focal plane.
source: TF uses a diffraction grating (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) to separate the spectral components of a pulsed laser beam, resulting in a temporally broadened pulse that is inefficient at excitation except at the focal plane, where the components are recombined.
evidence: This is a description of the temporal focusing method based on established knowledge of the technique and supported by citation to a figure showing the setup.

claim: Temporal focusing yields a volume of excitation in which the diameter in the x-y plane and the thickness in the axial plane are controlled independently.
source: This yields a volume of excitation in which the diameter in the x-y plane and the thickness in the axial plane are controlled independently (Oron et al., 2012, 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work by Oron et al.

claim: The excitation volume was designed to approach the dimensions of a typical neuronal soma.
source: We designed our excitation volume to approach the dimensions of a typical neuronal soma (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a methodological statement supported by reference to a figure showing the excitation volume dimensions.

claim: ChR2 fusion proteins were generated by attaching a 65 amino acid motif from the Kv2.1 voltage-gated potassium channel to the carboxy terminus of ChR2-EYFP.
source: To restrict expression of ChR2 to the soma and proximal dendrites, we generated ChR2 fusion proteins by attaching a 65 amino acid motif from the Kv2.1 voltage-gated potassium channel to the carboxy terminus of ChR2-EYFP (Lim et al., 2000).
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing construct generation, with citation to prior work on the Kv2.1 motif.

claim: Nontargeted ChR2-EYFP fluorescence was distributed throughout the processes of dissociated cortical neurons.
source: Nontargeted ChR2-EYFP fluorescence was distributed throughout the processes of dissociated cortical neurons that had been filled with a fluorescent dye (Figure 1A).
evidence: This observation is supported by data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Targeted ChR2-EYFP-Kv2.1 was located primarily in the soma and excluded from the axon and distal dendrites.
source: In contrast, targeted ChR2-EYFP-Kv2.1 was located primarily in the soma and excluded from the axon and distal dendrites (Figure 1A).
evidence: This observation is supported by data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The TF-stimulated current declined approximately 10-fold at 50 µm from the soma with the targeted construct.
source: The TF-stimulated current declined ~10-fold at 50 µm from the soma with the targeted construct, versus two fold for the non-targeted construct (Figure 1C; N=10 untargeted cells from four animals and N=13 targeted cells from six animals).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The TF-stimulated current declined approximately 2-fold at 50 µm from the soma with the non-targeted construct.
source: The TF-stimulated current declined ~10-fold at 50 µm from the soma with the targeted construct, versus two fold for the non-targeted construct (Figure 1C; N=10 untargeted cells from four animals and N=13 targeted cells from six animals).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Stimulation of cells expressing non-targeted ChR2 evoked currents up to 200 µm away from the neuronal soma.
source: Stimulation of cells expressing non-targeted ChR2-evoked currents up to 200 µm away from the neuronal soma, often delineating a pattern indicative of the dendritic arbor of the cell (Figure 1D).
evidence: This observation is supported by data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Cells expressing the targeted construct exhibited significant currents only when stimulated within the 25–50 µm immediately adjacent to the cell body.
source: In contrast, cells expressing the targeted construct exhibited significant currents only when stimulated within the 25–50 µm immediately adjacent to the cell body.
evidence: This is an observation from experimental data comparing targeted and non-targeted constructs.

claim: The lack of direct light-activated currents throughout much of the neuron's dendritic field makes it possible to visualize synaptic currents that would be evoked by ChR2 activation of nearby presynaptic neurons.
source: The lack of direct light-activated currents throughout much of the neuron's dendritic field makes it possible to visualize synaptic currents that would be evoked by ChR2 activation of nearby presynaptic neurons, even those that lie within the neuron's dendritic field.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations about reduced dendritic currents.

claim: Noticeable currents could be detected at distances of 50 µm or greater from the soma of cells expressing nontargeted ChR2 when stimulating along axonal processes.
source: Although the amount of detected current decreased rapidly for both constructs as TF stimulation was moved along the axon, noticeable currents could be detected at distances of 50 µm or greater from the soma of cells expressing nontargeted ChR2 (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This observation is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3B.

claim: Cells expressing targeted ChR2 demonstrated an 80% reduction of current when stimulating just 20 µm down the axon.
source: In contrast, cells expressing targeted ChR2 demonstrated an 80% reduction of current when stimulating just 20 µm down the axon and significantly less current than cells expressing nontargeted ChR2 throughout its examined length (Figure 1—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3C.

claim: The targeted ChR2 exhibited increased peak current amplitude in response to TF activation compared to nontargeted ChR2.
source: Interestingly, the targeted ChR2 also exhibited increased peak current amplitude in response to TF activation, presumably by concentrating channel density at the soma (Figure 2A; from 308.3 ± 43.5 pA in 12 nontargeted cells to 760.5 ± 146.0 pA in 12 targeted cells at 3.63 mW/µm2; p=0.0101 for main effect of targeting by two-way repeated measures ANOVA)
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data with statistical analysis.

claim: Targeted ChR2 exhibited over three-fold reduction of the power required to reach action potential threshold compared to nontargeted ChR2.
source: leading to an over three-fold reduction of the power required to reach action potential threshold (Figure 2B; from 2.75 ± 0.31 mW/µm2 in 17 nontargeted cells to 0.88 ± 0.23 mW/µm2 in 19 targeted cells; p=8.028 × 10–5 by Mann-Whitney U Test).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data with statistical analysis.

claim: At the threshold stimulation power for each cell, the amount of evoked current was similar between targeted and untargeted constructs.
source: At the threshold stimulation power for each cell, the amount of evoked current was similar between targeted and untargeted constructs (261.06 ± 31.62 pA for untargeted ChR2 and 222.70 ± 27.21 pA for targeted ChR2 p=0.3677 by two sample t-test)
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data with statistical analysis.

claim: The targeting modification had no effect on rheobase, other intrinsic physiological parameters, or action potential properties in response to current injections.
source: consistent with the observation that the targeting modification had no effect on rheobase, other intrinsic physiological parameters, or action potential properties in response to current injections (Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and Table 1.

claim: The full-width at half maximum of action potential generation was 11.1 µm laterally and 23.3 µm axially for targeted ChR2.
source: The full-width at half maximum of these measurements was 11.1 µm laterally and 23.3 µm axially (N=10 cells from 7 animals; Figure 2C and D).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data shown in Figure 2C and D.

claim: The full-width at half maximum of action potential generation was 19.6 µm laterally and 36.2 µm axially for nontargeted ChR2.
source: Similar measurements using nontargeted ChR2 demonstrated resolution of 19.6 µm laterally and 36.2 µm axially (N=13 cells from 5 animals; Figure 2C and D)
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data shown in Figure 2C and D.

claim: The mean latency from light onset to generation of a single action potential was 38.98 ± 17.33 ms.
source: In terms of temporal precision, the mean latency from light onset to generation of a single action potential in the above experiments was 38.98 ± 17.33 ms
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data.

claim: The average jitter (defined as the standard deviation of the latency across the ten trials for a given cell) was 6.8 ± 2.1 ms.
source: the average jitter (defined as the standard deviation of the latency across the ten trials for a given cell) was 6.8 ± 2.1 ms.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data.

claim: Increasing stimulation power beyond threshold provoked additional action potentials and eventually shortened the latency to first spike to 9.3 ± 1.8 ms.
source: Increasing stimulation power beyond threshold provoked additional action potentials and eventually shortened the latency to first spike to 9.3 ± 1.8 ms (Figure 2—figure supplement 2)
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The latency to first spike of 9.3 ± 1.8 ms is consistent with reported values for stimulating cortical neurons with sculpted light.
source: consistent with reported values for stimulating cortical neurons with sculpted light (Papagiakoumou et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by Papagiakoumou et al.

claim: Targeted ChR2-expressing cells exhibited shorter action potential latencies than nontargeted ChR2 cells at equivalent stimulation intensity.
source: Targeted ChR2-expressing cells exhibited shorter action potential latencies than nontargeted ChR2 cells at equivalent stimulation intensity, consistent with latency being power-dependent and the earlier observation that targeted ChR2 is more sensitive.
evidence: This is an observation from experimental data with inference about the mechanism.

claim: Temporal focusing pulses of 32 ms were effective at generating action potentials in opsin-expressing cells.
source: Temporal focusing pulses of 32 ms were effective at generating action potentials in opsin-expressing cells, and targeted ChR2 exhibited greatly enhanced photocurrents and lower power thresholds under these conditions (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: The combination of temporal focusing and soma-targeted ChR2 expression yields a highly reliable and spatially precise means to stimulate action potentials with somatic illumination.
source: Therefore, the combination of temporal focusing and soma-targeted ChR2 expression yields a highly reliable and spatially precise means to stimulate action potentials with somatic illumination.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented.

claim: A bicistronic AAV construct was generated encoding targeted ChR2-Kv2.1 followed by a P2A ribosomal skipping sequence and a histone 2B-mRuby2 fusion protein.
source: We generated a bicistronic adeno-associated virus (AAV) construct encoding targeted ChR2-Kv2.1 followed by a P2A ribosomal skipping sequence and a histone 2B-mRuby2 fusion protein to fluorescently label neuronal nuclei to identify cells for TF stimulation.
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing construct generation.

claim: The average stimulation power used in mapping experiments was 2.29 ± 0.55 mW/µm2.
source: For these experiments, we used an average stimulation power (2.29 ± 0.55 mW/µm2) that, when combined with a 150 ms stimulation pulse, frequently led to trains of 2–4 action potentials in the patched cells and facilitated detection of larger calcium transients.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data.

claim: The imaging power and dwell time did not lead to action potential generation in any cells recorded, instead causing an average inward current of 29.5 ± 9.5 pA.
source: We used an imaging power and dwell time that did not lead to action potential generation in any cells recorded, instead causing an average inward current of 29.5 ± 9.5 pA (N = 7 cells from 5 animals)—well below the average rheobase.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data.

claim: The average rate of detecting a calcium response to TF stimulation of a cell expressing the ChR2-Kv-P2A-H2B-mRuby2 bicistronic construct was 80.00 ± 2.60%.
source: In repeated experiments (seven neurons from five animals), another example of which is shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1, the average rate of detecting a calcium response to TF stimulation of a cell expressing the ChR2-Kv-P2A-H2B-mRuby2 bicistronic construct was 80.00 ± 2.60%.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data.

claim: The average connectivity rate was 10.27 ± 2.60% (27 connections out of 252 cells showing a calcium transient to photostimulation).
source: Overall, the average connectivity rate was 10.27 ± 2.60% (27 connections out of 252 cells showing a calcium transient to photostimulation)
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data.

claim: The connectivity rate measured with the optogenetic method was not significantly different from results using paired recording.
source: which was not significantly different from our own results using paired recording (7 connections out of 115 cells; Fisher's exact test, p=0.18).
evidence: This is a statistical comparison between two experimental methods.

claim: Direct responses from stimulation of the patched cell's dendritic arbor occurred during stimulation of 28.75 ± 4.46% of the target cells within a single field of view when using nontargeted ChR2.
source: Across the experiments, such direct responses occurred during stimulation of 28.75 ± 4.46% of the target cells within a single field of view.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data using nontargeted ChR2.

claim: Off-target calcium responses occurred with a probability of 15.17 ± 1.79% when using nontargeted ChR2.
source: These off-target responses occurred with a probability (the number of events divided by the number of target cells) of 15.17 ± 1.79%
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data using nontargeted ChR2.

claim: Off-target calcium events were observed at a significantly lower frequency in experiments with the targeted opsin (5.42 ± 1.39%, p<0.01 by two sample t-test).
source: Consistent with this interpretation, these off-target calcium events were observed at a significantly lower frequency in experiments with the targeted opsin (5.42 ± 1.39%, p<0.01 by two sample t-test).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data with statistical analysis.

claim: The average distance between a cell exhibiting an off-target calcium transient and the intended target cell was greater with nontargeted ChR2 (40.6 ± 6.4 µm versus 18.9 ± 2.4 µm; p<0.01 by two sample t-test).
source: Moreover, the average distance between a cell exhibiting an off-target calcium transient and the intended target cell was greater with nontargeted ChR2 (40.6 ± 6.4 µm versus 18.9 ± 2.4 µm; p<0.01 by two sample t-test)
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data with statistical analysis.

claim: The combination of TF and restricted ChR2 facilitated the mapping of local circuitry within the 300 µm surrounding a neuron without confounding signals from its dendritic arbor.
source: Our combination of TF and restricted ChR2 thus facilitated the mapping of local circuitry within the 300 µm surrounding a neuron without confounding signals from its dendritic arbor and with a higher throughput than that achieved with electrophysiological techniques alone.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented.

claim: Combining temporal focusing for two-photon activation of ChR2 with restriction of ChR2 expression to the soma and proximal dendrites of neurons yields a reliable method for evaluating synaptic connectivity with single-neuron resolution.
source: This study demonstrates that combining temporal focusing for two-photon activation of ChR2 with restriction of ChR2 expression to the soma and proximal dendrites of neurons yields a reliable method for evaluating synaptic connectivity with single-neuron resolution.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, supported by all the experimental data presented.

claim: The spatially restricted ChR2 expression allows unmasking of synaptic connections from neurons whose somata lie close to the dendrites of the postsynaptic cell.
source: The spatially restricted ChR2 expression we describe allows unmasking of synaptic connections from neurons whose somata lie close to the dendrites of the postsynaptic cell and would have been occluded by direct activation of ChR2 on the dendrite.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented.

claim: Depletion of ChR2 from axons prevents inadvertent depolarization of boutons or fibers of passage that could compromise attempts to identify the source of a synaptic event.
source: In addition, depletion of ChR2 from axons prevents inadvertent depolarization of boutons or fibers of passage that could compromise attempts to identify the source of a synaptic event.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing reduced axonal ChR2.

claim: ChR2 harboring the Kv2.1 localization motif showed enhanced sensitivity.
source: ChR2 harboring the Kv2.1 localization motif also showed enhanced sensitivity, which is of particular use in situations where excitation power is at a premium.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing lower power thresholds for targeted ChR2.

claim: The distribution of particular voltage-gated potassium channels defines a subcellular domain along the soma and proximal dendrites.
source: The distribution of particular voltage-gated potassium channels defines such a subcellular domain along the soma and proximal dendrites (Trimmer, 2015)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by Trimmer.

claim: A short Kv2.1 C-terminal sequence is sufficient for driving heterologous proteins to the soma and proximal dendrites region.
source: and the sufficiency of a short Kv2.1 C-terminal sequence for driving heterologous proteins to this region (Lim et al., 2000) made this strategy ideal for restricting ChR2 expression.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by Lim et al.

claim: Incorporating an ankyrin G binding motif into ChR2 drives its localization to the axon initial segment.
source: Although incorporating this motif into ChR2 drives its localization to the AIS (Grubb and Burrone, 2010; Wu et al., 2013)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: AIS-targeted ChR2 does not support light-generated action potentials under physiological conditions.
source: the resulting construct does not support light-generated action potentials under physiological conditions (Grubb and Burrone, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by Grubb and Burrone.

claim: AIS-targeted ChR2 alters the intrinsic firing properties of retinal neurons, presumably by displacing endogenous voltage-gated sodium channels.
source: Moreover, AIS-targeted ChR2 alters the intrinsic firing properties of retinal neurons, presumably by displacing endogenous voltage-gated sodium channels whose subcellular localization is also dependent on ankyrin G binding (Zhang et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by Zhang et al., with speculation about the mechanism.

claim: The Kv2.1 targeting strategy currently remains the optimal means of concentrating ChR2 such that action potentials will not be generated by TF stimulation of dendrites >20 µm away from the soma.
source: Therefore, the Kv2.1 targeting strategy currently remains the optimal means of concentrating ChR2 such that action potentials will not be generated by TF stimulation of dendrites >20 µm away from the soma.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data and comparison with alternative approaches.

claim: The Kv2.1 targeting approach has been successfully used with opsins to artificially generate center-surround receptive fields in retinal ganglion cells.
source: Indeed, this approach has been successfully used with opsins to artificially generate center-surround receptive fields in retinal ganglion cells (Wu et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by Wu et al.

claim: The Wu et al. (2013) study showed functional restriction of opsins to the soma and proximal dendrites by examining receptive field responses to wide (200 µm) bars of one-photon light.
source: The Wu et al. (2013) study showed functional restriction of opsins to the soma and proximal dendrites by examining receptive field responses to wide (200 µm) bars of one-photon light.
evidence: This is a description of prior work by Wu et al.

claim: The current study measured the somatic targeting at a finer scale than Wu et al. (2013).
source: We have now measured the somatic targeting at a finer scale, demonstrated two-photon excitation of targeted ChR2 that is enhanced relative to normal ChR2 under the same conditions, and established the utility of targeted opsins for enhancing the resolution of local connectivity maps of neural circuits.
evidence: This is an implicit comparison with prior work, inferred from the statement about measuring at a finer scale.

claim: The current study demonstrated two-photon excitation of targeted ChR2 that is enhanced relative to normal ChR2 under the same conditions.
source: We have now measured the somatic targeting at a finer scale, demonstrated two-photon excitation of targeted ChR2 that is enhanced relative to normal ChR2 under the same conditions, and established the utility of targeted opsins for enhancing the resolution of local connectivity maps of neural circuits.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings presented in the study.

claim: The current study established the utility of targeted opsins for enhancing the resolution of local connectivity maps of neural circuits.
source: We have now measured the somatic targeting at a finer scale, demonstrated two-photon excitation of targeted ChR2 that is enhanced relative to normal ChR2 under the same conditions, and established the utility of targeted opsins for enhancing the resolution of local connectivity maps of neural circuits.
evidence: This is a summary of the main contribution of the study.

claim: The soma-targeted ChR2 could be combined with many of the techniques for two-photon optical control of neuronal activity previously developed for caged neurotransmitters or optogenetic probes.
source: The soma-targeted ChR2 could be combined with many of the techniques for two-photon optical control of neuronal activity previously developed for caged neurotransmitters or optogenetic probes.
evidence: This is speculation about future applications of the method.

claim: The relative merit of the optical activation method depends on the axial resolution, temporal precision required and the number of neurons to be stimulated simultaneously in a given experimental paradigm.
source: The relative merit of the optical activation method depends on the axial resolution, temporal precision required and the number of neurons to be stimulated simultaneously in a given experimental paradigm.
evidence: This is a general statement based on knowledge of different optical methods.

claim: Rapid scanning of a diffraction-limited two-photon excitation spot in a pattern on the soma can generate action potentials.
source: For example, rapid scanning of a diffraction-limited two-photon excitation spot in a pattern on the soma can generate action potentials (Packer et al., 2012; Prakash et al., 2012; Rickgauer and Tank, 2009)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Combination of rapid scanning with spatial light modulators allows for simultaneous excitation of neuronal ensembles.
source: and combination with spatial light modulators allows for simultaneous excitation of neuronal ensembles (Packer et al., 2012, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The temporal resolution of the rapid scanning approach is limited by the time required to scan along the cell body.
source: The temporal resolution of this rapid scanning approach, however, is limited by the time required to scan along the cell body.
evidence: This is a statement based on knowledge of the rapid scanning method.

claim: Scanless activation of untargeted ChR in brain slices using TF is capable of generating action potentials in hippocampal pyramidal neurons within 1–3 ms of light onset.
source: Scanless activation of untargeted ChR in brain slices using TF, alone or in combination with spatial light modulators, is capable of generating action potentials in hippocampal pyramidal neurons within 1–3 ms of light onset (Andrasfalvy et al., 2010)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by Andrasfalvy et al.

claim: Scanless activation of untargeted ChR in brain slices using TF is capable of generating action potentials in cortical neurons in less than 10 ms.
source: and in cortical neurons in less than 10 ms (Papagiakoumou et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by Papagiakoumou et al.

claim: The minimization of action potential latency requires optimization of excitation area and laser power.
source: For experiments requiring temporal precision, the minimization of action potential latency requires optimization of excitation area and laser power (Papagiakoumou et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by Papagiakoumou et al.

claim: The reduced power required to bring soma-targeted opsins to threshold would be an asset to experiments requiring temporal precision or large numbers of neurons.
source: Because power is also the limiting factor in extending the area of two-photon activation to large numbers of neurons with spatial light modulators, the reduced power required to bring soma-targeted opsins to threshold would be an asset to such experiments.
evidence: This is an inference about the potential advantages of the method.

claim: The optimal performance of the method relies on sufficient co-expression of an opsin, a marker for opsin expression, and a genetically encoded calcium sensor.
source: The optimal performance of our method relies on sufficient co-expression of an opsin, a marker for opsin expression, and a genetically encoded calcium sensor.
evidence: This is a statement about the requirements for the method based on the experimental design.

claim: For GCaMP6s and similar sensors, there appears to be a balance between sufficient expression to detect single action potentials and excessive levels that lead to a lack of responsiveness.
source: For GCaMP6s and similar sensors, there appears to be a balance between sufficient expression to detect single action potentials and excessive levels that lead to a lack of responsiveness (Chen et al., 2013; Packer et al., 2015; Tian et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Heterogeneity in GCaMP expression levels between neurons with viral infection may be partially responsible for the 20% of neurons in which a change in GCaMP fluorescence was not detected with TF stimulation.
source: Indeed, heterogeneity in GCaMP expression levels between neurons with viral infection may be partially responsible for the 20% of neurons in which we did not detect a change in GCaMP fluorescence with TF stimulation.
evidence: This is speculation about the cause of the observation.

claim: Co-expression of GCaMP6s as the second member of a single P2A-mediated bicistronic construct resulted in lower than desired GCaMP6s expression level.
source: We have also explored the co-expression of GCaMP6s as the second member of a single P2A-mediated bicistronic construct, but the GCaMP6s expression level was lower than desired, resulting in inadequate detection of action potentials (data not shown).
evidence: This is a statement about experimental results that were not included in the main figures.

claim: Future development of these techniques will benefit from bypassing viral systems and instead expressing the calcium sensor or the opsin in transgenic animals.
source: Future development of these techniques will therefore benefit from bypassing viral systems and instead expressing the calcium sensor or the opsin in transgenic animals.
evidence: This is speculation about future improvements to the method.

claim: The enhanced sensitivity of the targeted ChR2 should alleviate the concern that there would be sufficient opsin expression from a single genetic locus for activation of neurons with two-photon excitation.
source: The enhanced sensitivity of the targeted ChR2 should alleviate the concern that there would be sufficient opsin expression from a single genetic locus for activation of neurons with two-photon excitation.
evidence: This is an inference about the implications of the enhanced sensitivity finding.

claim: The somatic targeting approach could be exploited in the context of other opsins such as C1V1.
source: The somatic targeting approach could also be exploited in the context of other opsins such as C1V1, which has recently been leveraged for two-photon stimulation of neural circuits in acute slices and in vivo (Packer et al., 2012, 2015; Prakash et al., 2012; Rickgauer et al., 2014).
evidence: This is speculation about future applications, with citations to prior work on C1V1.

claim: ReaChR is a good candidate for somatic targeting due to its sensitivity.
source: Other molecules which may be good candidates for somatic targeting include the red-shifted ReaChR for its sensitivity (Lin et al., 2013)
evidence: This is speculation about future applications, with citation to prior work on ReaChR.

claim: Chronos is a good candidate for somatic targeting due to its rapid temporal characteristics.
source: and Chronos for its rapid temporal characteristics (Klapoetke et al., 2014).
evidence: This is speculation about future applications, with citation to prior work on Chronos.

claim: The somatic restriction of membrane-bound genetically encoded voltage sensors could dramatically reduce background associated with the neuropil and facilitate an all-optical version of the current method.
source: Moreover, the somatic restriction of membrane-bound genetically encoded voltage sensors could dramatically reduce background associated with the neuropil and facilitate an all-optical version of our current method.
evidence: This is speculation about future applications of the targeting approach.

claim: The Kv2.1 targeting sequence is unable to restrict the distribution of the single-pass membrane protein CD8.
source: Because the Kv2.1 targeting sequence is unable to restrict the distribution of the single-pass membrane protein CD8, however, there may be certain structural constraints on the effectiveness of the motif (Lim et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by Lim et al.

claim: For the opsins, which are all seven transmembrane domain proteins likely to have a similar structure, the Kv2.1 motif will likely be sufficient to achieve somatic localization.
source: We suspect that at least for the opsins, which are all seven transmembrane domain proteins likely to have a similar structure, the Kv2.1 motif will be sufficient to achieve somatic localization.
evidence: This is speculation based on knowledge of opsin structure.

claim: The combination of TF and soma-restricted ChR2 enables functional connectivity mapping and is straightforward and easy to implement with standard two-photon microscopes.
source: In summary, our combination of TF and soma-restricted ChR2 enables functional connectivity mapping and is straightforward and easy to implement with standard two-photon microscopes.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the method.

claim: These techniques could be used in vivo, where the enhanced resolution of the targeted ChR2 makes it especially attractive for selective cell stimulation in behavioral paradigms.
source: Furthermore, these techniques could also be used in vivo, where the enhanced resolution of the targeted ChR2 makes it especially attractive for selective cell stimulation in behavioral paradigms.
evidence: This is speculation about future applications of the method.

claim: These enhancements to probing brain microcircuitry through optical stimulation promise to reveal much about nervous system function and how it might be modified by experience and perturbed in animal models of neurologic or psychiatric disease.
source: These enhancements to probing brain microcircuitry through optical stimulation promise to reveal much about nervous system function and how it might be modified by experience and perturbed in animal models of neurologic or psychiatric disease.
evidence: This is speculation about the potential impact of the method.

claim: Two-photon activation of single neurons with ChR2 is complicated by its kinetics and low single-channel conductance.
source: First, two-photon activation of single neurons with ChR2 is complicated by its kinetics and low single-channel conductance.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge about ChR2 properties.

claim: A diffraction-limited spot does not activate sufficient channels simultaneously to reliably bring neurons expressing ChR2 to action potential threshold.
source: A diffraction-limited spot does not activate sufficient channels simultaneously to reliably bring neurons expressing ChR2 to action potential threshold.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge about ChR2 activation.

claim: Rapid scanning of a diffraction-limited two-photon excitation spot across an opsin-expressing cell allows sufficient temporal integration to generate action potentials.
source: Rapid scanning of a diffraction-limited two-photon excitation spot across an opsin-expressing cell allows sufficient temporal integration to generate action potentials (Packer et al., 2012; Prakash et al., 2012; Rickgauer and Tank, 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Scanless two-photon excitation by temporal focusing increases the number of simultaneously excited opsin molecules by expanding the beam in the imaging plane without sacrificing the optical sectioning of multiphoton microscopy.
source: Alternatively, scanless two-photon excitation by temporal focusing (Oron et al., 2005; Zhu et al., 2005) increases the number of simultaneously excited opsin molecules by expanding the beam in the imaging plane without sacrificing the optical sectioning of multiphoton microscopy (Andrasfalvy et al., 2010; Losonczy et al., 2010; Papagiakoumou et al., 2010; Rickgauer et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The implementation of diffractive optical elements has allowed for more complicated excitation profiles that encompass multiple spots around a cell, ensembles of neurons, or particular branches of dendritic trees.
source: The implementation of diffractive optical elements (Fino and Yuste, 2011; Nikolenko et al., 2007; Packer and Yuste, 2011) or spatial light modulators (Dal Maschio et al., 2010; Nikolenko et al., 2008; Packer et al., 2012, 2015; Papagiakoumou et al., 2010, 2009, 2008) has also allowed for more complicated excitation profiles that encompass multiple spots around a cell, ensembles of neurons, or particular branches of dendritic trees.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The ability to use optogenetic stimulation to selectively target single neurons remains challenging because the opsins are expressed throughout the dendritic and axon terminal fields.
source: While these approaches have made it possible to provide sufficient two-photon illumination to reliably drive action potentials, the ability to use optogenetic stimulation to selectively target single neurons remains challenging because the opsins are expressed throughout the dendritic and axon terminal fields, generating a potential confounding source of light-induced electrical responses.
evidence: This is a statement about a limitation of existing optogenetic methods.

claim: It can be difficult to know whether a recorded electrophysiological event is due to stimulation of a presynaptic cell or 'direct' stimulation of a portion of the recorded cell's dendritic arbor.
source: For example, it can be difficult to know whether a recorded electrophysiological event is due to stimulation of a presynaptic cell or 'direct' stimulation of a portion of the recorded cell's dendritic arbor.
evidence: This is a statement about a challenge in interpreting optogenetic mapping experiments.

claim: Large amplitude direct responses may obscure simultaneous smaller synaptic events.
source: Although these possibilities can be distinguished by their kinetics, large amplitude direct responses may obscure simultaneous smaller synaptic events.
evidence: This is a statement about a limitation of existing methods.

claim: There is an indeterminate region of any circuit 'map' coinciding with the dendritic arbors of the recorded neuron, which can extend for 200 µm or more around the soma.
source: This essentially leaves an indeterminate region of any circuit 'map' coinciding with the dendritic arbors of the recorded neuron, which can extend for 200 µm or more around the soma.

claim: The optogenetic approach could be compromised by unintended activation of fibers of passage or local axonal boutons.
source: In addition, the optogenetic approach could be compromised by unintended activation of fibers of passage or local axonal boutons, which are known to respond to temporal focusing of two-photon excitation (Andrasfalvy et al., 2010; Losonczy et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Exclusion of opsins from axonal compartments has previously been achieved by fusing the opsin with targeting domains that bind to myosin Va motors necessary for transporting proteins into dendrites.
source: Exclusion of opsins from axonal compartments has previously been achieved by fusing the opsin with targeting domains that bind to myosin Va motors necessary for transporting proteins into dendrites; one such motif from melanophilin is sufficient to exclude ChR2 from axons and enhance the resolution of neural circuit maps (Lewis et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by Lewis et al.

claim: ChR2 fused with a melanophilin motif remains distributed throughout the dendritic tree and does not solve the problem of undesired direct activation of a neuron's processes while trying to stimulate other neurons in close proximity.
source: The resulting ChR2 distribution, however, remains throughout the dendritic tree and thus does not solve the problem of undesired direct activation of a neuron's processes while trying to stimulate other neurons in close proximity.
evidence: This is a statement about a limitation of the melanophilin targeting approach.

claim: The Kv2.1 potassium channel has a particularly unique localization to clusters at the neuronal soma and proximal dendrites.
source: Our alternative targeting approach took advantage of the Kv2.1 potassium channel, which has a particularly unique localization to clusters at the neuronal soma and proximal dendrites (Trimmer, 1991)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by Trimmer.

claim: The Kv2.1 localization is achieved through a 66-amino acid domain in its C-terminus.
source: achieved through a 66-amino acid domain in its C-terminus (Lim et al., 2000)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by Lim et al.

source: that drives its association with myosin IIb and specific post-Golgi transport vesicles destined for the somatic compartment (Jensen et al., 2014).

claim: The Kv2.1 targeting signal is sufficient to alter ChR2 trafficking in retinal ganglion cells.
source: Furthermore, this targeting signal is sufficient to alter ChR2 trafficking in retinal ganglion cells (Wu et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by Wu et al.

claim: The approach allows robust and precise activation of neurons in brain slices for the construction of functional synaptic connectivity maps with single-cell resolution without loss of information about local connections in the region of the dendritic arbor of the recorded neuron or inadvertent activation of axons.
source: Our approach allows robust and precise activation of neurons in brain slices for the construction of functional synaptic connectivity maps with single-cell resolution without loss of information about local connections in the region of the dendritic arbor of the recorded neuron or inadvertent activation of axons.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings and advantages of the method.
